summary: Theodor Benfey was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. and habilitation at the University of Göttingen. He spent his career there as a Privatdozent (1834), Lehrmeister (1848), and Ordinarius (1862–1881).

Theodor Bloch was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at the University of Leipzig under Ernst Windisch from around 1888 to 1892. He also studied under Georg Bühler from roughly 1893 to 1895 as a Specialschüler.

Theodor Goldstücker was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Königsberg and Bonn under Peter von Bohlen, Karl Rosenkranz, Christian Lassen, and Eugène Burnouf. He later served as professor of Sanskrit at University College London and University of London.

Theodor Nöldeke was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar, linguist, and religious studies specialist. He studied at Göttingen, Vienna, Leiden, and Berlin, later serving as professor at Kiel (1864, 1868–1872) and Strasbourg (1872–1906).

Theodor Zachariae was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Hermann Sauppe, Theodor Benfey, Georg Curtius, and Hermann Brockhaus. He held posts as professor at the University of Greifswald (1883) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1890–1921).

Theodore Dwight Woolsey worked in linguistics and other fields. After studying at Hopkins School, Yale College, and Princeton University, he served as president of Yale University from 1831 to 1871 and president of the American Oriental Society from 1853 to 1863.

Theodore Riccardi was an Indologist and linguist. He held a post at Columbia University (attested 1974–1976 and 1990) and served as guest editor for the Journal of the American Oriental Society in 1989.

Theodore Riccardi Jr. is a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He served on the faculty at Columbia University, where he is attested as a faculty member in 2014 and Professor Emeritus in 2026.

Theodore Stcherbatsky was a specialist in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev, Georg Bühler, and Hermann Jacobi. He was attested as a member of the Russian Academy of Sciences from 1927 to 1931.
Theodorus Willem Juynboll was a religious studies scholar who studied at Leiden University between approximately 1885 and 1893. In 1916, he held a post at Utrecht University.
Theophil Gubler, who worked in Indology and linguistics, studied under Jacob Wackernagel and completed his doctoral degree at the University of Basel in 1903.
Thibaut d'Hubert is an Indologist who held a post at the University of Chicago and is attested as a Vertretungsprofessor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

Thich Nhat Hanh was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at Báo Quốc Temple, Saigon University, Princeton, and Columbia. He held posts at Columbia, Princeton, Cornell, and Vạn Hạnh University.
Thich Thien Nghiem is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. at the University of Delhi, attested in 2012, under the supervision of Shalini Singhal.

Thierry Mathou is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He studied at EDHEC Business School and Sciences Po, and served as an associated political scientist at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique around 1993.

Thierry Meynard is a sinologist and philosopher who earned his Ph.D. at Peking University under Yulie Lou. He served as professor of philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University (around 2006) and director of The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies (2012).

Thinh Canh Quang is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Ph.D. at the University of the West, attested in 2007, under doctoral supervisor Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya and teachers Lewis Lancaster and Ananda Guruge.

Thinlay Ram Shashni is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. At the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, he served as an editor (attested 1997, 2007) and as Associate Professor, IN-charge/HoD (attested 2026).

Thinley Dorji Bhutia was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and chief editor of Bulletin of Tibetology in 1994, and as a teacher at Darjeeling Government High School.

Thinley Norbu Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Mindrolling Monastery and under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (Dudjom Rinpoche). He also founded the White Lotus School.
